builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Local and Sparse Kernel Operator Learning for Incompressible Flows: An Operator Lagrange Formulation
summary: The method replaces global output reconstruction and dense operator regression with local divergence-free interpolants solved in parallel on GPUs and sparse operator regression using compactly supported kernels. It requires one sparse solve per new input and fits the kernel support radius to data to control sparsity, though local coefficients are never explicitly formed. Validation depends on careful selection of sparsity patterns and support radii; performance degrades if the kernel support is misfitted or if the flow regime lacks sufficient local training data.
rationale: This is a specialized numerical method for incompressible flow simulation rather than a general LLM optimization technique, making it relevant only if the reader works specifically on computational fluid dynamics or scientific machine learning with PDE constraints.
technique: Local Sparse Kernel Operator Learning for Flows

claims.statement: The method replaces global output reconstruction and dense operator regression with local divergence-free interpolants solved in parallel on GPUs and sparse operator regression using compactly supported kernels. It requires one sparse solve per new input and fits the kernel support radius to data to control sparsity, though local coefficients are never explicitly formed. Validation depends on careful selection of sparsity patterns and support radii; performance degrades if the kernel support is misfitted or if the flow regime lacks sufficient local training data.

Affine augmentation lowers error by more than an order of magnitude for forced isotropic turbulence; Lagrange evaluation is up to nearly three orders of magnitude more accurate than direct evaluation with global reconstructions.
